name: Anthony van Dyck
findings: Uses raisin black 2.0x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 954 paintings here).
Uses smoky black 2.0x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 954 paintings here).
Uses dark walnut 1.8x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 954 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, oxblood turns up as a small accent in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 2.7x the archive's rate (from 954 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, yew green turns up as the lightest note in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 4.6x the archive's rate (from 954 paintings here).
Pairs olive-buff with putty more than chance would predict (4 of 954 paintings here).
Pairs honey yellow with ochre brown more than chance would predict (5 of 954 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, raisin black, black) covers 60% of his paintings here.
